solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pleasant housing over the way, within budget

indicators.note: housing means holding something inside, so the pleasant word encloses the rest

parts.note: pleasant means affable, friendly
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
RD, short for road, a way

explanation.surface: An estate agent praises nice homes across the road that cost little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' is the container signal, not homes; O is the cricket over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something within budget costs no more than one can pay, i.e. is cheap enough to buy.

clue.text: Roughly speaking, computer program is awesome!

parts.note: an app is a computer program, short for application
rox is slang spelling of rocks, meaning is awesome

explanation.surface: An excited user gushes that some software is great, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation of approximately is used to mean roughly or about.

clue.text: Ensign attached to vessel

parts.note: an ensign is a flag
on means attached, as a lid is on

explanation.surface: A naval flag is fastened to a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large jug or bottle for wine or cider, a drinking vessel.

clue.text: Important letter greeted Sir Liam at work

indicators.note: at work means busy, being worked on, so the letters of greeted sir liam are rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight named Liam was welcomed at his office with a key letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuable letter would be sent by a postal service with a signed receipt and tracking.

clue.text: Old college to adapt, admitting two graduates

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the adapting word holds the graduates inside

parts.note: to adapt is to alter
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate, so two of them give MA twice

explanation.surface: A former college changes to let in a couple of graduates.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'nourishing mother', it names the school or university a person attended.

clue.text: Base swear-word uttered in this place

indicators.note: uttered means spoken aloud, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: base means low, and a swear-word is a cuss

explanation.surface: Someone says a vulgar oath right here.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is Latin for a position or site, used in English for a particular location.

clue.text: Exclamation suppressed by William, George and Andrew?

indicators.note: suppressed by means held down within, so the exclamation sits inside the name's short form

parts.note: WM is the traditional abbreviation of the name William
HA is a cry of triumph or laughter

explanation.surface: A royal-sounding list of princes whose cry has been stifled.
explanation.walkthrough: George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley formed the 1980s pop duo; the princely names pull toward royalty, and 'suppressed by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The two pop stars were the members of that 1980s duo, so the question mark signals a definition by example.

clue.text: Gloria working to host band in satellite appearance?

indicators.note: to host means to hold as a guest, so the glory word encloses the band

parts.note: a gloria is a halo or aureole, as painted around a saint's head
FM is a radio frequency band
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A woman named Gloria is working to host a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloria' looks like a name or hymn; here it is a halo.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon, our satellite, appears as a semicircle at its first and last quarters.

clue.text: Wise men about to look at radio tuner

parts.note: the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity
C is circa, about
to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: The Three Wise Men gather round to examine a wireless set.
explanation.definitionFit: Old valve radios had a glowing indicator tube that showed when a station was correctly tuned in.

clue.text: Chap booked to be on island by Friday

definitions.text: Chap booked to be on island by Friday

parts.words: Chap booked to be on island by Friday
parts.note: booked suggests a reservation, but means a man in a book; Friday is his companion, not the weekday

explanation.surface: A man reserves a trip to an island, departing by the end of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friday' reads as a deadline but is Defoe's character Man Friday, castaway's companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's novel hero is shipwrecked on an island where he meets his servant Friday.

clue.text: Jogged with PG Tips, causing an accident

indicators.note: with here means the tips go along either side of the jogging word, wrapping it
tips are the ends, so the outer letters of PG are taken

parts.note: jogged means ran

explanation.surface: A runner drinking a famous British tea brand somehow crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: PG Tips is a well-known British tea brand; here 'Tips' means the ends of PG, and 'with' wraps them round the jogging word.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is British slang for a minor crash, especially of a car or aircraft.

clue.text: Bug truncated record tweet, possibly

indicators.note: truncated means cut short, so the bug word loses its final letter

parts.note: a bug is a germ, a microbe
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A shortened account about a computer glitch, perhaps posted online.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short online post, so Twitter is an example of a platform for brief blogging.

clue.text: Marsupial suggested by Eliot's feline versifier?

indicators.note: suggested by means only hinted at, so the first word of the name is cut down to its initial

parts.note: Old Possum is the persona behind T.S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats

explanation.surface: A pouched animal is hinted at by the poet who wrote about cats.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats is the source of the musical Cats; 'suggested by' shortens 'Old' to O.
explanation.definitionFit: The American pouched mammal is a marsupial, carrying its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Shaky's half-seen with one's microphone

indicators.note: half of the word seen means its first two letters

parts.note: one's is I'S, one being I
MIC is the short form of microphone

explanation.surface: A nervous singer only half-sees, clutching the mic.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthquakes shake the ground, so seismic describes trembling, shaky movement.

clue.text: Early Conservative cuddling daughter, perhaps 9

indicators.note: cuddling means hugging, holding inside, so the early word wraps the daughter letter

parts.note: betimes is an old word for early
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory dad cuddles his daughter early in the evening, reading to her.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to ROBINSON CRUSOE, one book that might be read at night. 'cuddling' puts D inside BETIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's novel is an example of a tale read to a child at night, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Make fresh start to embrace political party in a mess

indicators.note: a fresh start to means a new first letter, so the embrace word has its opening letter replaced

parts.note: to embrace is to cuddle
the first letter of make supplies the new opening
DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A politician urges a new beginning for a party alliance in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' gives its first letter M to replace the C of CUDDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Muddled up describes things confused or jumbled, a disorderly state.

clue.text: The lads going on tour, taking in Northern isles

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the shuffled letters hold the northern letter
going on tour means travelling around, so the letters of the lads are rearranged

explanation.surface: A group of young men go on a trip to some Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going on tour' makes SHETLAD of THE LADS; 'taking in' adds N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shetlands are the northernmost Scottish island group.

clue.text: Testing time to manage introducing Arab currency

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in, so the currency goes between the other pieces

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
the rial is the currency of Saudi Arabia, Oman and Yemen

explanation.surface: An economist tests how long it takes to bring in a Gulf currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or experiment to see if something works is a test.

clue.text: Hard bargaining disrupted North Sea rig, restricting commencement of drilling

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the shuffled letters enclose the starting letter
disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of north sea rig are rearranged
commencement of means the first letter of drilling

explanation.surface: An offshore oil platform is disrupted while drilling starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' turns NORTHSEARIG into HORSETRAING; 'restricting' places D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd, tough negotiation is likened to haggling over the sale of a horse.

clue.text: Fed up with American English? Calm down!

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read upwards, so the word fed is turned backwards

explanation.surface: Someone sick of American English is told to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: To defuse a situation is to ease tension, reduce its danger.

clue.text: Ring round unknown hotel as 3 is delivered

indicators.note: round means going around, so the ring word encloses the other letters

parts.note: a band is a ring, as a wedding band
Y is a mathematical unknown
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A ring goes round a mystery hotel as an important letter is sent.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is REGISTERED MAIL, which is handed over in person.
explanation.definitionFit: A registered letter is given personally to the recipient, who signs for it.

clue.text: Catch streetcar No.1 of Metropolitan eastern line

parts.note: a streetcar is a tram

indicators.note: No.1 of means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A traveller catches the first Metropolitan streetcar on the eastern line.
explanation.definitionFit: A trammel is a kind of fishing net, and as a verb it means to snare or entangle, i.e. catch.

clue.text: Drunk, going topless for game

indicators.note: topless means without its top, so the first letter of the drunk word goes

parts.note: blotto is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: An intoxicated reveller strips off for a bit of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery or a bingo-like game of chance.

clue.text: Theft of Brie reportedly ending in acrimony

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the actress's surname is taken by sound

parts.note: Brie Larson is the American actress who starred in Captain Marvel

indicators.note: ending in means the last letter of acrimony

explanation.surface: A cheese theft ends in bitter recrimination.
explanation.walkthrough: Brie looks like the French cheese but is the actress Brie Larson, whose surname sounds like LARCEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for stealing property, so it is theft.

clue.text: Relieved by flying ace, I flirted outrageously

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace, as on playing cards

indicators.note: outrageously means wildly, scandalously, so the letters of i flirted are rearranged

explanation.surface: A flying ace confesses he has been relieved after shameless flirting.
explanation.definitionFit: A besieged city relieved by aircraft has supplies or people carried in or out by air.

clue.text: With which one gets tanked up in holiday dive?

definitions.text: With which one gets tanked up in holiday dive?

parts.words: With which one gets tanked up in holiday dive?
parts.note: tanked up suggests drunk in a seedy bar, but the tanks are air cylinders worn underwater

explanation.surface: A tourist getting drunk in a scruffy holiday bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dive' and 'tanked up' point to a bar and drinking; really the diver wears air tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-contained underwater breathing apparatus is the gear divers strap on, with air cylinders on the back.

clue.text: European future pilot abandoning port in Tanzania

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the port letters drop out of the pilot's name

parts.note: Dan Dare, Pilot of the Future, was the hero of the Eagle comic
Dar, short for Dar es Salaam, the Tanzanian port

explanation.surface: A trainee pilot leaves an East African harbour behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare was a famous British comic-strip space hero of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Denmark is a Scandinavian, and so a European.

clue.text: Gather hempen cord in knots

indicators.note: in knots means tangled up, so the letters of hempen cord are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gathers up a hemp rope that is all tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather, in the sense of 'I gather', is to understand or grasp.
